summary.text: A 7-day-old male born full term by normal vaginal delivery to a mother with systemic lupus erythematosus, hypothyroidism and group B streptococcus presented to the ED with cough and difficulty breathing, was found to have RSV and was discharged. The next day he returned with decreased activity, decreased oral intake and a reported choking episode with weak extremities.

He was admitted for investigation; the lumbar puncture was refused by the parents. An irregular heart rhythm noted on the ECG monitor during EEG was read as incomplete heart block. The mother had undisclosed SLE, prompting an NLE workup. EEG showed regional disturbance with a low seizure threshold; antibody testing showed positive anti-U1RNP-70kD with negative anti-Ro/SS-A and anti-La/SS-B.

Levetiracetam and empiric cefotaxime and ampicillin were started for possible meningitis. Echocardiogram and brain CT angiogram were normal; Holter monitoring showed sinus slowing with junctional escape beats and marked sinus bradycardia. He remained stable and afebrile in the PICU without a pacemaker and was discharged on oral levetiracetam.

Two weeks later there was no seizure recurrence or new symptoms and cardiac tests had improved. A month after discharge a repeat EEG was normal and levetiracetam was discontinued. At 6 months of age he was meeting developmental milestones with a normal examination; the parents refused repeat laboratory testing.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the two figures are inspected in visual.json.
Table 1 hematocrit is labelled Low and potassium High while the text says the complete blood count and renal function were within normal range; the CBC and renal summary statements are review_only.

Mother's SLE, hypothyroidism, GBS, antibiotics and Table 2 antibody results are recorded in the index record with subject mother; Table 3 and other literature-review content are not index-patient facts.
No time is borrowed for table results or follow-up sentences; ordering relations are only those stated by the quotes.

Unlabelled "the mother was found to have GBS ... received antibiotics" and the later "mother received one dose of IV antibiotics in this admission" are kept as separate items because the source does not equate them.
ANA keeps flag positive (titre, text "positive speckled"); ENA keeps flag high (numeric CU value with printed High in Table 1 and "ENA was high" in the discussion).
